mainEntity.name: How much does an Audi A4 S4 3.0 TDI / TFSI engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: The cost to replace an Audi A4 S4 3.0 TDI / TFSI engine typically ranges from £4,500 to £8,500 for a rebuilt unit, depending on the specific V6 architecture and whether you choose supply-only or supply & fit.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of supercharger failure in an Audi A4 S4 3.0 TFSI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common symptoms include a distinct marbles-in-a-can rattling noise from the engine bay on deceleration, a noticeable loss of boost pressure, and an illuminated engine management light.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in an Audi A4 S4 3.0 TDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the vehicle is in good overall condition and valued above £8,000, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine is a cost-effective alternative to buying a new car.

mainEntity.name: How long does an Audi A4 S4 3.0 TDI / TFSI engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A professional supply & fit service for the Audi A4 S4 3.0 TDI / TFSI typically takes 2 to 3 days.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the CCWA and CREC engine codes in the Audi A4 S4?

acceptedAnswer.text: The CCWA is the 3.0L V6 TDI (diesel) engine used in the B8 generation (2009-2012), producing 240-245hp. The CREC (and CGWC) is the 3.0L V6 TFSI (petrol) supercharged engine used in the B8.5 and B9 generations (2013-present), producing 333hp.

historyTimeline.h2: Audi A4 S4 3.0 TDI / TFSI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance

CREC / CGWC, 3.0L V6 TFSI Supercharged (333hp), carried forward into the B9 generation with refined engine management and emissions controls.

commonProblems.h2: Audi A4 S4 3.0 TDI / TFSI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Audi A4 S4 3.0 TDI / TFSI is a high-performance executive vehicle, but its complex V6 architecture introduces specific failure points. The CCWA (diesel) and CGWC/CREC (petrol) engine codes dominate replacement demand for this variant. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Oil Cooler Seal Leaks - Why the Audi A4 S4 3.0 TDI (CCWA) Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The O-ring seals on the oil cooler, located deep in the V of the engine, degrade over time due to heat cycles, leading to significant oil loss and potential catastrophic engine damage if ignored.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove intake manifold, replace oil cooler O-rings, flush system
repairOptions.longevity: Highly recommended as a preventative or early-stage repair

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Necessary only if oil starvation has caused bearing or timing chain damage

problems.recommendation: For the 3.0 TDI, if the issue is purely an oil cooler leak, a specialist seal replacement is the most cost-effective first step. However, if the engine has suffered oil starvation, a rebuilt unit is required. For the 3.0 TFSI, a rebuilt engine assembly with an updated supercharger coupler and revised cooling components is the most reliable long-term solution to restore factory performance.

problems.h4: Supercharger Coupler & Cooling Failures - Why the Audi A4 S4 3.0 TFSI (CGWC/CREC) Wears Prematurely
problems.affectedModels: Audi A4 S4 3.0 TDI / TFSI (CGWC, CREC, 2013-present)
problems.rootCause: The internal supercharger coupler wears out, causing a distinct rattling noise and loss of boost, compounded by brittle plastic coolant crossover pipes that are prone to cracking and leaking.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace supercharger snout/coupler and plastic coolant pipes
repairOptions.longevity: Highly recommended to prevent overheating and restore performance

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: The right call when overheating has caused head gasket failure or internal damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: - Vehicle worth under ~£5,000: repair or used engine typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit. - Vehicle worth ~£5,000-£8,000: evaluate both; reconditioned is viable if keeping the car 2+ years. - Vehicle worth ~£8,000-£15,000: reconditioned/rebuilt usually justifies the premium via warranty and reliability. - Vehicle worth £15,000+: replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value. A typical B8 Audi A4 S4 3.0 TDI (2009-2012) currently falls into the £6,000-£14,000 band, making a reconditioned replacement a viable option if you plan to keep the vehicle, though it approaches the watch threshold. Newer B8.5 and B9 Audi A4 S4 3.0 TFSI models (£12,000-£35,000) comfortably absorb the replacement cost, making a rebuilt unit the financially sound choice.
problems.recommendation: For the 3.0 TDI, if the issue is purely an oil cooler leak, a specialist seal replacement is the most cost-effective first step. However, if the engine has suffered oil starvation, a rebuilt unit is required. For the 3.0 TFSI, a rebuilt engine assembly with an updated supercharger coupler and revised cooling components is the most reliable long-term solution to restore factory performance.
